html:
A German friar and professor of theology whose protest against the church began the Protestant Reformation.

Born at Eisleben in Saxony, he studied law, but after a terrifying thunderstorm in 1505 he became an Augustinian friar. As a professor at Wittenberg he came to believe that people are saved by faith in God's grace, not by good works or church rituals.

In 1517 he wrote his 95 Theses against the sale of indulgences, which promised less time in purgatory for money. Thanks to the press of Gutenberg, his writings spread across Germany within weeks. He was excommunicated in 1521, and at the Diet of Worms, before the emperor Charles V, he refused to take back his words. Declared an outlaw, he was hidden at the Wartburg castle, where he translated the New Testament into German.

His German Bible shaped the German language. He married a former nun, Katharina von Bora, and wrote hymns. In the Peasants' War of 1525 he sided with the princes, and his late writings against the Jews were vicious. The Catholic answer came at the Council of Trent.
sum: A German friar and professor of theology whose protest against the church began the Protestant Reformation.
